overview: SSE plc is a UK-listed electricity company (LSE, GBP reporting, fiscal year ending 31 March) that invests in, develops, builds and operates the infrastructure and generation needed for a cleaner, more secure and more affordable energy system. Its portfolio spans economically-regulated electricity transmission and distribution networks in the north of Scotland and central southern England (SSEN Transmission, SSEN Distribution), onshore/offshore wind and hydro renewables generation (SSE Renewables), and flexible thermal generation, gas storage and energy trading/supply (SSE Thermal, SSE Energy Markets, Energy Customer Solutions). SSE operates almost entirely in Great Britain and the island of Ireland and is currently mid-way through a five-year, £33bn capital investment programme (FY2026-FY2030) weighted roughly 80% to regulated UK electricity networks.

business_model.summary: SSE earns a blend of highly-visible, index-linked regulated network revenue (Ofgem price controls RIIO-T2/T3 and RIIO-ED2/ED3, allowed on a Regulated Asset Value (RAV) that is itself inflation-linked) and market-exposed earnings from renewables generation (subsidised via CfDs/ROCs plus merchant power sales), flexible thermal generation (Capacity Market payments plus wholesale/balancing revenue) and energy supply/trading to business and Irish retail customers. Management targets ~80% of Group EBITDA being index-linked by FY2030 as the networks share of capital and earnings grows, which is the central thesis of the current investment plan.

revenue_streams.name: SSEN Transmission (regulated networks, N. Scotland, 75% SSE / 25% Ontario Teachers')
SSEN Distribution (regulated networks, N. Scotland & central-southern England)
SSE Renewables (onshore/offshore wind, hydro, pumped storage, batteries)
SSE Thermal (flexible CCGT generation, gas storage, Capacity Market)
Energy Customer Solutions (B2B energy supply GB, B2B/B2C Ireland via SSE Airtricity)

business_model.customer_type: Mixed: regulated-utility 'customers' are Ofgem and network end-users (effectively captive, no competition) in Networks; B2B and government counterparties (CfD/Capacity Market) in Renewables and Thermal; B2B and B2C energy supply customers in GB and Ireland via Energy Customer Solutions
business_model.geographic_mix: UK and Ireland only (Great Britain networks/generation, island of Ireland energy supply); no material US/Asia/continental Europe operations

competitive_position.market_position: SSEN Transmission is one of only a handful of licensed electricity transmission owners in GB (natural regional monopoly in the north of Scotland) and one of the fastest-growing regulated networks in Europe; SSEN Distribution is one of 14 GB distribution network operators (regional monopoly, ~4m customers); SSE Renewables is among the largest developers of UK/Irish offshore and onshore wind (co-developer of Dogger Bank, the world's largest offshore wind farm, and the consented 4.1GW Berwick Bank); SSE Thermal operates some of the most efficient flexible CCGT plant in Europe

moat_factors.description: SSEN Transmission and SSEN Distribution hold exclusive regional electricity licences; Ofgem price controls (RIIO) guarantee allowed returns on RAV with no realistic new entrant risk

RAV and allowed revenues are substantially inflation-linked, providing earnings visibility and protection against cost inflation as the networks share of the business grows toward ~80% of EBITDA by FY2030

moat_factors.factor: Scale and pipeline in UK/Irish renewables
moat_factors.description: Large consented pipeline (Dogger Bank phases, Berwick Bank up to 4.1GW) and long operating track record, but subject to competitive CfD auctions and merchant price risk

moat_factors.factor: Asset irreplaceability / high barriers to entry
moat_factors.description: Transmission and distribution networks and large consented offshore wind sites cannot be readily replicated given planning, consenting and grid-connection constraints

moat_factors.factor: Flexible thermal fleet as system back-up
moat_factors.description: Capacity Market contracts and dispatchable gas/storage assets provide a hedge against renewables intermittency and are increasingly valuable as the system decarbonises

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on continued political/regulatory support for the energy transition; net-zero consensus is fragmenting in the UK
Capital-intensive, debt-funded model exposed to interest-rate and gilt-yield movements
Renewables output and merchant power/gas trading earnings remain weather- and commodity-price dependent despite hedging
Smaller customer-facing supply business (Energy Customer Solutions) has limited scale versus large retail suppliers
Execution risk from a trebling of capex and an unprecedented pipeline of 11 major transmission projects running concurrently

growth_drivers: RIIO-T3 (accepted by SSEN Transmission, effective 1 April 2026) and upcoming RIIO-ED3 (business plan due December 2026) price controls, expected to grow combined Networks RAV from £15.6bn (FY2026) toward ~£40bn gross by FY2030

£33bn five-year investment plan (FY2026-FY2030): ~80%/£27bn into regulated UK electricity networks (SSEN Transmission ~£22bn, SSEN Distribution ~£5bn) and ~20%/£6bn selectively into Renewables (~£4bn) and Flexibility (~£2bn)

SSEN Transmission RAV targeted to grow at a ~30% CAGR to ~£30bn by FY2030 as the 11 major north-of-Scotland grid reinforcement projects (including Eastern Green Link 2/3, Orkney Link, Skye Reinforcement) are built

Renewables capacity build-out toward ~9GW installed by FY2030 (from ~5GW in FY2025), led by Dogger Bank (phases A/B generating, phase C under construction) and the consented 4.1GW Berwick Bank (Phase B secured a 20-year CfD in AR7; FID targeted 2027)

Electrification of the UK economy (EVs, heat pumps, data centres, industrial decarbonisation) driving rising demand for network connections and capacity, particularly in SSEN Distribution's southern England licence area
Adjusted EPS CAGR guidance of 10-13% FY2026-FY2030 to 225-250p, underpinned by ~80% index-linked EBITDA by FY2030
Progressive dividend policy targeting 5-10% per annum DPS growth off a 64.2p FY2025 base
Potential ~£2bn of targeted asset rotation (partial stake sales) later in the plan to help fund capex without over-levering the balance sheet

business.description: 11 concurrent major transmission projects plus offshore wind construction; residual risk rated High/High by SSE's own Principal Risk framework given project scale, complexity and supply chain/consenting dependencies

SSE competes globally for turbines, cables, HVDC converters and specialist labour amid a worldwide clean-energy build-out; tariff volatility and Middle East conflict have added cost and lead-time pressure

business.risk: Renewables output and merchant price variability
business.description: Wind/hydro output and wholesale power/gas prices affect Renewables and Thermal profits despite SSE's rolling 36-month hedging programme; FY2026 renewables profit growth was partly offset by lower hedged prices and mixed weather

business.risk: Loss of senior leadership / organisational change
business.description: New CEO (Martin Pibworth) and CFO in post less than two years, alongside a Group Operating Model and Efficiency Review that has driven departures of senior colleagues and a measurable decline in the employee engagement index (78% vs 86% prior year)

financial.risk: Elevated leverage amid a trebling of capex
financial.description: Adjusted net debt and hybrid capital of £10.1bn at FY2026 (3.3x net debt/EBITDA); management guides net debt/EBITDA to stay below 4.5x through the plan, but the funding mix relies on continued debt issuance, ~£2bn of further equity-economics from asset rotation, and a cost of debt that rose to 4.1% (avg.) as cheaper debt rolls into more expensive issuance
UK gilt rate volatility directly affects SSE's borrowing costs on a balance sheet growing toward incremental tens of billions of pounds of debt and hybrid capital over the plan
The November 2025 £2bn equity placing lifted shares in issue from 1,106.3m to 1,212.2m, directly reducing adjusted EPS guidance from an original 175-200p FY2027 range to 168-193p

financial.risk: FX / cross-currency exposure on hybrid and euro debt
financial.description: SSE and SSEN Transmission have issued euro-denominated hybrid bonds and a euro Green Bond, hedged via cross-currency swaps, but mark-to-market swings on these instruments flow through reported (not adjusted) results

regulatory.description: In April 2026 the UK Government extended and increased the Electricity Generator Levy from 45% to 55% on low-carbon generation revenues above a threshold, directly taxing SSE Renewables and SSE Thermal profits

While RIIO-T3 has now been accepted as 'investable and deliverable', SSEN Distribution's RIIO-ED3 business plan (due December 2026) and the next transmission reset remain exposed to Ofgem's totex/WACC/incentive settings, with Ofgem itself flagging possible changes to the Totex Incentive Mechanism and gearing

regulatory.risk: Political fragmentation on net zero / affordability backlash
regulatory.description: UK public opinion (68% YouGov survey) now prioritises lower bills over net zero; the Government has already cut household bills via green-levy removal (~£150) while simultaneously raising the EGL, illustrating the political cross-currents SSE's networks/renewables-led model is exposed to

Of 34 major transmission consents required, 25 secured by FY2026; several (including Cambushinnie) have faced legal challenge or Scottish Government appeal, risking schedule slippage on ASTI/LOTI projects

regulatory.risk: Cyber security and critical infrastructure regulation
regulatory.description: Rated High likelihood/High impact; heightened nation-state and ransomware threat levels following high-profile UK corporate cyber incidents, with increasing regulatory reporting obligations

macro.description: The 2026 Middle East conflict (and the ongoing Russia/Ukraine war) have driven gas and oil price spikes that raise input costs, consumer energy bills and Energy Affordability Principal Risk materiality

macro.risk: UK inflation and gilt market volatility
macro.description: UK inflation rose to 3.3% in the year, raising nominal debt service costs even as it also lifts inflation-linked RAV and allowed revenues
Storms (Floris, Amy, Eowyn) damage network assets and disrupt supply, while mixed wind/hydro resource years directly affect Renewables output and profit
UK consumer energy debt rose ~20% over 2025, increasing political pressure for intervention that could affect network charges or supplier economics

macro_factors.industry_outlook: UK and Irish electricity demand is expected to rise materially this decade as electrification (EVs, heat pumps, data centres, industrial decarbonisation) accelerates, driving an unprecedented, multi-decade grid investment cycle; renewable generation reached a record 52.5% share of UK electricity in 2025, reinforcing the structural case for continued network reinforcement and offshore wind build-out, even as political support for net zero becomes more contested
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate: regulated Networks earnings are largely non-cyclical and index-linked; Renewables/Thermal/Energy Markets earnings have moderate exposure to commodity cycles, weather and wholesale power price swings, partially mitigated by multi-year hedging and Capacity Market/CfD contracts
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high given a heavily debt- and hybrid-capital-funded £33bn capex programme; higher-for-longer UK rates raise financing costs on new debt issuance (average cost of debt already up from 4.0% to 4.1%) though RAV-linked allowed returns provide some offset
key_input_costs: Grid/HVDC cable and converter station materials and labour
Offshore wind turbines, foundations and installation vessels
Natural gas (thermal generation feedstock and hedging)

recent_developments.event: Trading update: H1 FY2027 adjusted EPS guided to 64-68p; regulated networks investment up ~70% YoY in H1, renewables output up ~20% YoY on favourable weather; full-year FY2027 guidance of 168-193p adjusted EPS and FY2030 guidance of 225-250p both reiterated; H1 capex ~£2.5bn, adjusted net debt and hybrid capital expected ~£11.5bn

FY2026 full-year results: adjusted EPS 153.5p (down 5% YoY on dilution from the equity raise), adjusted operating profit £2,236.6m, record capex of £3.6bn (+20% YoY), final dividend 47.3p taking full-year DPS to 68.7p (+7%); net debt/EBITDA stable at 3.3x; SSEN Transmission accepted Ofgem's RIIO-T3 Final Determination

Announced transformational £33bn five-year investment plan to FY2030 (trebling capex, ~80% to regulated networks) alongside a £2bn equity placing; shares rose sharply (reported up ~10-12% on the day) as the market welcomed removal of balance-sheet funding uncertainty

UK Government extended and increased the Electricity Generator Levy from 45% to 55% in response to Middle East conflict-driven energy market volatility, while separately removing ~£150 of green levies from average household bills from autumn 2025

Leadership transition: Martin Pibworth's first full year as Chief Executive, working alongside CFO Barry O'Regan; departures of several senior long-serving colleagues alongside new executive hires in IT, Procurement, Legal, Sustainability and Business Development; Group Operating Model and Efficiency Review largely completed (exception: ongoing SSEN Distribution transformation programme), with £84.7m of restructuring exceptional charges in FY2026
Berwick Bank Phase B secured a 20-year Contracts for Difference agreement for 1.4GW in CfD Allocation Round 7 (AR7), ahead of a targeted Final Investment Decision in 2027

SSEN Transmission issued a €750m, eight-year Green Bond to help fund the £22bn north-of-Scotland transmission investment programme; SSE remains the largest UK corporate issuer of Green Bonds (£5.1bn outstanding)

Analyst sentiment broadly positive: Berenberg (Buy, GBX 2,980 target), Jefferies (Buy, GBX 3,060), Deutsche Bank (Buy, GBX 2,650); consensus 'Moderate Buy' with an average target around GBX 2,600-2,700 against a share price near GBX 2,490 (market cap ~£30-31bn)

guidance.as_of: Trading Update, 1 October 2026 (reiterating FY2026 Annual Report / 27 May 2026 guidance)

items.notes: Equivalent to the original 175-200p target set in 2023, mechanically adjusted down for dilution from the November 2025 £2bn equity placing; reiterated at the 1 October 2026 trading update
Lower seasonal H1 weighting reflects a growing proportion of regulated networks earnings; given at the 1 October 2026 trading update
Implies a 10-13% adjusted EPS CAGR FY2026-FY2030, underpinned by ~80% of EBITDA being index-linked by FY2030
Up from £3.6bn in FY2026 (which itself was a record, +20% YoY); phasing consistent with the £33bn five-year plan; H1 FY2027 capex tracking ~£2.5bn, ~70% higher YoY in regulated networks
~80%/£27bn to regulated UK electricity networks (SSEN Transmission ~£22bn, SSEN Distribution ~£5bn); ~20%/£6bn to Renewables (~£4bn) and Flexibility (~£2bn), including ~£3bn currently uncommitted
Off an unaltered 64.2p FY2025 baseline; FY2026 DPS of 68.7p represented a 7% increase; scrip dividend retained, capped at 25% take-up with buyback offset if needed

FY2026 actual was 3.3x; management expects leverage to rise but stay within this ceiling, supported by ~£2bn of targeted asset rotation later in the plan and continued investment-grade credit ratings (reaffirmed post plan announcement)
From £8.955bn (100% basis) at FY2026; implies ~30% CAGR; management sees potential for more RAV growth beyond FY2030 as NESO reassesses reinforcement needs
From £15.6bn at FY2026 (100% basis); SSEN Distribution RAV targeted at £9-10bn by FY2030 (~10% CAGR)
From ~5GW at FY2025; selective/disciplined growth, not a 'build at all costs' target

items.target: SSEN Transmission significantly higher; SSEN Distribution similar; SSE Renewables similar; SSE Thermal significantly higher (Capacity Market step-up); Energy Customer Solutions lower
items.notes: As set out in the FY2026 Annual Report (27 May 2026); all expectations explicitly subject to normal weather, market conditions and plant availability

guidance.management_commentary: CFO Barry O'Regan: the FY2027 earnings forecast is 'unchanged since 2023' once adjusted for the equity raise, and full-year capex is expected to exceed £5bn, 'in line with the phasing of the £33bn investment plan.' At the 1 October 2026 trading update, management reiterated both FY2027 and FY2030 EPS ranges despite H1 seasonality shifting toward networks, citing continued strong delivery across the 11 major transmission projects and renewables output up ~20% YoY on favourable weather. CEO Martin Pibworth has emphasized that the Group's 'carefully integrated portfolio offers resilience in most market scenarios' amid geopolitical volatility (Middle East conflict) and UK net-zero policy fragmentation.

bull_case: Unique, low-risk earnings mix: ~80% of EBITDA index-linked and regulated-monopoly by FY2030, giving unusually high visibility into a 10-13% adjusted EPS CAGR and 5-10% DPS growth through FY2030 for a FTSE 100 utility

Structural, multi-decade UK grid investment supercycle (electrification, data centres, EVs, Clean Power 2030) with SSEN Transmission RAV guided to grow ~30% CAGR and combined Networks RAV to roughly treble to ~£40bn by FY2030

Funding uncertainty resolved: the November 2025 £33bn plan and £2bn equity placing were well received by the market and reaffirmed by credit rating agencies, removing a key overhang that had weighed on the shares

World-leading, de-risked renewables pipeline: Dogger Bank (A generating, B/C progressing) and the 4.1GW consented Berwick Bank (Phase B already CfD-contracted) provide visible medium-term growth with government-backed, inflation-linked CfD pricing
Resilient business mix across Networks/Renewables/Flexibility means SSE can perform 'in most market scenarios,' cushioning macro, political and commodity-price shocks relative to single-segment peers
bear_case: Execution risk is unusually high: 11 concurrent major transmission projects plus large offshore wind construction, against a backdrop of global supply-chain and skilled-labour competition for the same materials and contractors as every other country's energy transition

Rising political/regulatory headwinds: the Electricity Generator Levy was just raised from 45% to 55%, UK net-zero political consensus is fragmenting (68% of the public prioritise lower bills over net zero), and future RIIO-ED3/next-T-price-control settlements are not yet locked in

Leverage is set to keep rising through the plan (net debt/EBITDA already 3.3x, guided to stay below but approach 4.5x) in a higher-for-longer UK rate environment, with average cost of debt already ticking up to 4.1%

EPS dilution risk is real and recurring: the FY2026 equity raise already cut adjusted EPS guidance (175-200p to 168-193p) and reported EPS fell 2% even as operating profit grew, and further funding levers (asset rotation, more debt) carry their own execution and market-timing risk

Earnings remain partly exposed to weather and commodity volatility (renewables output, hedged power/gas prices) and to one-off/non-recurring items that have made recent-year segment profit comparisons volatile (e.g., SSEN Distribution's -54% operating profit YoY from a prior-year inflation true-up)
